chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to do, specifically for one who died from Banu Hashim, something that he did not do for any of the Muslims. When he performed salat over the Hashimi and sprinkled his grave with water, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would place his palm upon the grave until his fingers could be seen in the clay. Then a stranger would arrive, or a traveler from the people of al-Madinah, and would see the new grave with the mark of the palm of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم upon it, and would say: Who has died from the family of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم?

key_terms.آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: the family of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.بَنِي هَاشِمٍ: Banu Hashim, the clan of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.صَلَّى عَلَى الْهَاشِمِيِّ: performed funeral salat over a deceased Hashimi

ai.seo_question: What special practice did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم perform for the graves of deceased members of Banu Hashim?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a distinctive practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم toward the deceased of Banu Hashim. After the funeral salat and sprinkling the grave with water, he would place his palm upon the grave, leaving a visible mark that identified the deceased as being from the family of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.
